idea-plugin.description:
Queue up Claude Code tasks and let them run in your IDE terminal while you work.
  • TODO / In progress / Done board — drag cards to reorder or to start them.
  • Tasks run in a real Claude Code terminal, so you can watch and step in at any time.
  • Pick which terminal a task runs in — a new tab, one the plugin opened, or a shell you opened yourself.
  • Completion is detected automatically and the next task starts on its own.
  • Tasks in different terminal tabs run in parallel; within one tab they run in order.
Requires the claude CLI on your PATH.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.6.6

  • Sending a task to a conversation that's still answering no longer collides with it. The queue waits for that turn to finish, then sends — before, the task could be marked done the moment the earlier answer ended, and the next one started too early.
  • Long prompts are submitted properly. A large paste ended up sitting in Claude's input box without running, because the Enter arrived as part of the pasted text.

0.6.5

  • New Recent conversations button on the toolbar. It lists this project's recent Claude conversations with the title Claude gave them, how full their context is, and when you last used them — pick one and it resumes in the terminal you choose. If it's already open in a tab, you're taken there instead.

0.6.4

  • Renamed to Claude Task Queue — the old name was too generic to find. Same plugin, nothing to reinstall.

0.6.3

  • Each terminal's column now shows how full that conversation's context is. Hover the column title for the exact figure — 598.6k/1m (60%) and the model it's measured against. The title turns amber past 60% and red past 80%, so you can see a conversation filling up before it compacts.
  • Fixed: opening the tool window could fail with an internal error.
  • Fixed: on setups where the project path goes through a symlink, the plugin looked for transcripts in the wrong place — so answers and context never showed up.

0.6.2

  • Fixed the declared minimum IDE version — 2025.3, which is where the reworked terminal this plugin drives first appears.

0.6.1

  • Requires 2025.3 or newer now. The reworked terminal — the default engine since 2026.1 — only exists from 2025.3, and supporting it is what makes tab reuse work on a default setup.
  • Right-click a selection in the editor and "Add to Task Queue" now fills the task input with the file, line range and code, ready for you to type what to do — instead of a one-line dialog you couldn't edit.
  • Renaming a terminal tab renames its column too. Titles that Claude Code sets itself are ignored, so every tab doesn't end up with the same name.
  • The running task is marked with a border that gently pulses, and a card that just moved is outlined instead of tinted — easier to read the text on it.
  • Cards show more of the prompt before cutting it off, with the full text on hover.
  • Finished tasks are listed newest first.
  • Fixed: dragging a task onto a terminal's column failed with "That terminal tab is gone" unless you had run something in that tab first.

0.6.0

  • Tasks in different terminal tabs now run at the same time. Within a tab they still run one after another, so a conversation keeps its order — but two tabs no longer wait for each other.
  • IN PROGRESS is split into one column per terminal tab, each in its own colour, so you can see what every conversation is working on at a glance. Drag a waiting card onto another tab's column to move it there — it starts right away if that tab is free.
  • Columns follow your open terminals, so they stay put instead of appearing and disappearing as tasks come and go.

0.5.0

  • Works with the new Reworked terminal — the default engine on 2026.1. Until now the plugin could only see Classic terminal tabs, so on a default 2026.1 setup your open tabs were ignored and a new one was opened every time. Picking an existing tab, detecting whether claude is already running in it, and sending prompts all work on both engines now.
  • New tabs on the Reworked engine start without being brought to the front, so the queue no longer has to show the terminal to get a task going.

0.4.5

  • If your open terminal tabs can't be used, the plugin now says so instead of quietly opening a new tab. This happens with the Reworked terminal engine (the default on 2026.1) — switch to Classic in Settings → Tools → Terminal to reuse your own tabs.

0.4.4

  • Starting a task no longer steals your keyboard focus, so the queue moving on to the next task won't drag you away from whatever you were doing. Opening a brand-new tab still shows the terminal — it has to be visible for the session to start — but your focus stays put. Double-click a card when you do want to jump to its terminal.

0.4.3

  • Each project now has its own queue, so a task running in one project no longer blocks another — start a run in project A and keep working in project B. Your board only shows that project's cards. Queues from earlier versions are not carried over.
  • Interrupted a task in the terminal? A ↻ button on the card re-sends it to the same conversation, so it picks up where you cut it off. Interrupting no longer leaves the card stuck until the timeout.
  • Waiting tasks get ↻ too — deleting the running task used to strand them in IN PROGRESS with no way to start them.
  • The input box is cleared before a task is re-sent, so leftover typing can't run together with the prompt.
  • Removed the toolbar log button: the log was wiped whenever a task started, so it never held the run you wanted to look at.

0.4.1

  • Running every TODO in a new conversation now uses a single terminal tab and runs them one after another, so they share context instead of opening a tab each.
  • Long prompts wrap onto more lines on a card — the run/edit/delete buttons no longer get pushed out of view.

0.4.0

  • Stop now leaves the running task alone and moves waiting tasks back to TODO, instead of marking them done while claude keeps working.
  • Type multi-line tasks — Enter adds, Shift+Enter breaks the line, and the Up arrow in an empty field opens your recent prompts.
  • Card buttons are ordered run, edit, delete, with bigger click targets.
  • Roomier board: a separator under each column header and more vertical padding.

0.3.1

  • Fixed: a terminal tab where you started claude yourself was rejected as "busy running something else".

0.3.0

  • Finished cards show claude's answer, so you don't have to open the terminal to see what happened. Notifications carry it too.
  • Running cards show elapsed time, updated every second.
  • Keyboard shortcuts on the board: Delete to remove, Cmd+Enter to run, F2 to edit.
  • Notifications go to the OS notification center instead of an IDE popup.

0.2.0

  • Run a task in any terminal tab — a new one, one the plugin opened, or a shell you opened yourself. If claude isn't running there yet, the plugin starts it.
  • Task completion is detected automatically and the next task starts on its own.
  • Drag cards to reorder them or to start them. Inline actions on each card (edit, run, delete) and a running-task card takes you to its terminal.
  • Notifications when a task finishes and when the queue drains.

action.description: Queue the selection or file as an automated task
